subproblems.title: Extension of currents from U to ℝ^P by a smooth cutoff equal to 1 near a compact K ⊆ U
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and K ⊆ U compact. Then there is a map E : 𝒟_{m+1}(U) → 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn U (m+1) → GeometricCurrentOn univ (m+1)) such that: (i) for every X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) and every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ K, (E X)(ω) = X(ω), where ω is regarded as a test form on ℝ^P (testFormOnInclusion); (ii) if X_j ⇀ X in U then E X_j ⇀ E X in ℝ^P; (iii) M(E X) ≤ M(X) for every X (total masses: massOn ℝ^P and massOn U, Simon 6.2.4–6.2.5); (iv) if X(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) whose topological support is disjoint from K, then spt(E X) ⊆ K and M(∂(E X)) ≤ M(∂X); (v) if some IMRep R in U represents X and R.carrier ⊆ K, then E X is integer multiplicity in ℝ^P. (In the proof E X(ω) = X(ζω) for one fixed smooth cutoff ζ.)

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent-supplied proof of cbr_closure_succ, step 8 (extension to ℝ^P: T̂(ω) := T(ζω) with a cutoff ζ ∈ C^∞_c(U) equal to 1 near K) together with the facts used in steps 9–11 (IM transfer, support, mass and boundary-mass bounds, weak convergence, agreement with the original current on forms supported in K). The vanishing hypothesis in (iv) replaces the appeal to (VO) in step 8: it is exactly what (VO) yields from spt X ⊆ K, and the localization child supplies it directly.

1. (Cutoff.) ℝ^P is locally compact and regular, so (Mathlib exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure) there is an open V₁ with K ⊆ V₁, closure V₁ compact and closure V₁ ⊆ U, and then an open V₂ with closure V₁ ⊆ V₂, closure V₂ compact and closure V₂ ⊆ U. By the smooth Urysohn lemma in finite-dimensional real normed spaces (Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff with smoothness order ∞, s := V₂ open, t := closure V₁ closed, t ⊆ s) there is a C^∞ function ζ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with support ζ = V₂ and ζ(x) = 1 for all x ∈ closure V₁. Hence K₂ := tsupport ζ = closure V₂ is compact with K₂ ⊆ U, and ζ = 1 on the open set N := V₁ ⊇ K.
2. (Multiplication by ζ.) For a k-form ω on ℝ^P let ζω be x ↦ ζ(x)ω(x). If ω is a test form (C^∞, compact support), then ζω is C^∞ (product of C^∞ maps), support(ζω) ⊆ support ω so ζω has compact support, and tsupport(ζω) ⊆ tsupport ζ ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ K₂ ⊆ U. Thus ω ↦ ζω is a linear map M_k : 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) → 𝒟^k(U) (pointwise it is additive and commutes with scalars).
3. (Norm homogeneity.) For c ∈ ℝ and a k-covector α, the Euclidean coefficient norm satisfies |cα| = |c|·|α|: every coefficient α(e_I), I strictly increasing, is multiplied by c, so the sum of squares is multiplied by c² and its square root by |c|. Hence |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x implies |(ζω)(x)| = ζ(x)|ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
4. (Continuity of M_k.) Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) (TestFormOnConverges): there is a compact K' with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K' for all j and, for every l ∈ ℕ, D^l ω_j → 0 uniformly on K'. Then tsupport(ζω_j) ⊆ K₂ for all j, tsupport 0 = ∅ ⊆ K₂, and K₂ is a compact subset of U. Fix i ∈ ℕ. For x ∉ K' we have x ∉ tsupport ω_j, so D^l ω_j(x) = 0 for every l (the support of the l-th derivative lies in tsupport ω_j, Mathlib support_iteratedFDeriv_subset); hence ε_{j,l} := sup_{x ∈ ℝ^P} ‖D^l ω_j(x)‖ = sup_{x ∈ K'} ‖D^l ω_j(x)‖ → 0 as j → ∞, for each l. Each D^l ζ is continuous with compact support, so B_l := sup_x ‖D^l ζ(x)‖ < ∞. By the Leibniz estimate (Mathlib norm_iteratedFDeriv_smul_le, in Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Bounds), for every x, ‖D^i(ζω_j)(x)‖ ≤ Σ_{l=0}^{i} C(i,l)‖D^l ζ(x)‖‖D^{i−l}ω_j(x)‖ ≤ Σ_{l=0}^{i} C(i,l) B_l ε_{j,i−l}, and the right side tends to 0. Since D^i 0 = 0, D^i(ζω_j) → D^i 0 uniformly on K₂. So M_k(ω_j) → 0 in 𝒟^k(U), with the compact set K₂.
5. (Definition of E.) For X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) put (E X)(ω) := X(ζω) = X(M_{m+1}ω), ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P). E X is linear, and if ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) then M_{m+1}ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^{m+1}(U) (step 4), so (E X)(ω_j) → 0 by the continuity of X. Thus E X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P).
6. (Proof of (i).) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ K. For x ∈ K, ζ(x) = 1; for x ∉ K, x ∉ tsupport ω and ω(x) = 0. So ζω = ω pointwise; the inclusion into 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) does not change the underlying form, hence M_{m+1}(ιω) = ω in 𝒟^{m+1}(U) and (E X)(ιω) = X(ω).
7. (Proof of (ii).) If X_j ⇀ X in U then (E X_j)(ω) = X_j(ζω) → X(ζω) = (E X)(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P).
8. (Proof of (iii).) If ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) is admissible for M(E X) (|ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x), then ζω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) is admissible for M_U(X) (steps 2–3), so ofReal((E X)(ω)) = ofReal(X(ζω)) ≤ M_U(X) = M(X). Taking the supremum over ω gives M(E X) ≤ M(X).
9. (Proof of (iv), support.) Assume X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅. Let x ∉ K. As K is closed there is ε > 0 with ball(x, 2ε) ∩ K = ∅; let W := ball(x, ε). Then closure W ⊆ closedBall(x, ε) ⊆ ball(x, 2ε), so closure W is compact, contained in ℝ^P and disjoint from K. For ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, tsupport(ζω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W is disjoint from K, so (E X)(ω) = X(ζω) = 0. Hence W lies in the zero region of E X and x ∉ spt(E X). Therefore spt(E X) ⊆ K.
10. (Proof of (iv), boundary mass.) Under the same assumption let η ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with |η(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. By definition ∂(E X)(η) = (E X)(dη) = X(ζ dη). For y ∈ N the forms ζη and η coincide on the neighbourhood N of y, so their derivatives at y coincide, and since the exterior derivative at y depends only on the derivative at y (SimonGMT's exteriorDerivative is Mathlib's extDeriv, and Mathlib Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq applies), d(ζη)(y) = dη(y) = ζ(y)dη(y). Hence δ := d(ζη) − ζdη, a test form in 𝒟^{m+1}(U) (ζη ∈ 𝒟^m(U) and d maps 𝒟^m(U) into 𝒟^{m+1}(U); ζdη = M_{m+1}(dη)), vanishes on N; so support δ ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N, a closed set, whence tsupport δ ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N is disjoint from K ⊆ N, and X(δ) = 0. Therefore ∂(E X)(η) = X(ζdη) = X(d(ζη)) = ∂X(ζη). As ζη ∈ 𝒟^m(U) is admissible for M_U(∂X) (step 3), ofReal(∂(E X)(η)) ≤ M_U(∂X) = M(∂X); taking the supremum, M(∂(E X)) ≤ M(∂X).
11. (Proof of (v).) Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in U representing X with M ⊆ K. Let R̂ have the same carrier, multiplicity and orientation, regarded in ℝ^P. All IMRep fields that do not mention the domain are unchanged (M Borel and countably (m+1)-rectifiable, θ measurable and ≥ 1 on M, ξ a.e. strongly measurable for H^{m+1}⌞M and orienting the approximate tangent spaces of M a.e.), M ⊆ ℝ^P trivially, and for every compact K' ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫_{M∩K'} θ dH^{m+1} ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^{m+1} < ∞, because M ∩ K' ⊆ M = M ∩ K and K is a compact subset of U (local integrability field of R). So R̂ is an IMRep in ℝ^P. For ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P), (E X)(ω) = X(ζω) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ζ(x)ω(x)) dH^{m+1}(x) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^{m+1}(x) = R̂.action(ω), since ζ = 1 on M ⊆ K (the integrands agree on M). Hence R̂ represents E X and E X is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Smooth cutoff ζ: ℝ^P → [0,1] with tsupport ζ compact ⊆ U and ζ = 1 on an open N ⊇ K (Mathlib exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure, exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff).
ω ↦ ζω maps 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) linearly into 𝒟^k(U), keeps |ω| ≤ 1, and is sequentially continuous by the Leibniz estimate norm_iteratedFDeriv_smul_le.
E X := X(ζ·) is a current in ℝ^P; weak convergence passes through E.
ζω = ω when tsupport ω ⊆ K, so E X agrees with X there; M(E X) ≤ M(X).
If X vanishes off K: spt E X ⊆ K, and d(ζη) − ζdη vanishes on N, so ∂(E X)(η) = ∂X(ζη) and M(∂E X) ≤ M(∂X).
An IMRep in U with carrier in K, regarded in ℝ^P, represents E X because ζ = 1 on the carrier.

subproblems.title: Mass localization for a current vanishing away from a compact set (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U, V, C ⊆ ℝ^P with C compact, V open and C ⊆ V, and let X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U k) satisfy X(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) whose topological support is disjoint from C. Then M_G(X) ≤ M_V(X) for every set G ⊆ ℝ^P, where M_W(X) = X.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (Simon 6.2.5). In particular, taking G := U, M(X) = M_U(X) ≤ M_V(X).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U V C : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k), IsCompact C → IsOpen V → C ⊆ V → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k)) C → X ω = 0) → ∀ G : Set (Euclid P), X.massOn G ≤ X.massOn V
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused declaration: this is the already comparator-accepted theorem lcmp_massOn_le_of_vanish_off_compact (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.local_comparison-a1.mass_localization-a1), reused here with its identical frozen Lean type; in the present decomposition it is step 5 of the parent-supplied proof of cbr_closure_succ (“Z_{j,r}(ω) = Z_{j,r}(χω) ≤ M_G(Z_{j,r}) with χ ∈ C_c^∞(G; [0, 1]) equal to 1 near the slicing sphere”), stated for an arbitrary current X, compact set C and open set V, and for every G. The numbered proof is the one reviewed for that node.

Notation: |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a k-covector (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm); ω is admissible for M_G if ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; M_G(X) is the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over admissible ω.

1. Case C = ∅. Every test form has support disjoint from ∅, so X(ω) = 0 for all ω; every term of the supremum defining M_G(X) is ofReal(0) = 0, so M_G(X) = 0 ≤ M_V(X).
2. Assume C ≠ ∅. Choose δ > 0 with {x : dist(x, C) ≤ δ} ⊆ V (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open) and let V′ := {x : dist(x, C) < δ/2}. V′ is open, C ⊆ V′, and closure(V′) ⊆ {x : dist(x, C) ≤ δ/2}, a compact set (closed thickening of a compact set in the proper space ℝ^P) contained in V.
3. A smooth cut-off. Take g ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P) with values in [0, 1] and {g ≠ 0} = V′ (Mathlib IsOpen.exists_contDiff_support_eq). g is continuous and positive on the nonempty compact set C ⊆ V′, so a := min_C g > 0 (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn). Let τ := Real.smoothTransition (smooth, 0 ≤ τ ≤ 1, τ = 0 on (−∞, 0], τ = 1 on [1, ∞)) and χ(x) := τ(2g(x)/a). Then χ is smooth and 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1. On the open set N := {g > a/2} ⊇ C we have 2g/a > 1, so χ = 1 on N. Where g = 0 we have χ = τ(0) = 0, so {χ ≠ 0} ⊆ V′; hence tsupport χ ⊆ closure(V′) ⊆ V and χ has compact support.
4. Scaling of the norm. For c ∈ ℝ and a k-covector α, |cα| = |c|·|α|: the coefficients of cα on the increasing coordinate tuples are c times those of α, so the sum of their squares is c² times that of α, and √(c²s) = |c|√s.
5. Let ω be admissible for M_G and put ω₁ := χω, ω₂ := ω − ω₁ = (1 − χ)ω. ω₁ is smooth (product of smooth maps) and tsupport ω₁ ⊆ tsupport ω ∩ tsupport χ; hence ω₁ has compact support contained in U, i.e. ω₁ ∈ 𝒟^k(U), and tsupport ω₁ ⊆ V. By step 4, |ω₁(x)| = χ(x)|ω(x)| ≤ 1. So ω₁ is admissible for M_V and ofReal(X(ω₁)) ≤ M_V(X).
6. ω₂ ∈ 𝒟^k(U) vanishes on the open set N, because χ = 1 there. Every point of C has the neighbourhood N on which ω₂ ≡ 0, so no point of C lies in tsupport ω₂ = closure{ω₂ ≠ 0}; i.e. tsupport ω₂ is disjoint from C, and the hypothesis gives X(ω₂) = 0. By linearity X(ω) = X(ω₁) + X(ω₂) = X(ω₁), hence ofReal(X(ω)) ≤ M_V(X).
7. Taking the supremum over all admissible ω gives M_G(X) ≤ M_V(X). ∎
proof_key_steps: C = ∅: X vanishes identically, so M_G(X) = 0.
Smooth χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on an open N ⊇ C and compact tsupport χ ⊆ V: χ = τ(2g/a) with {g ≠ 0} = V′ ⋐ V and a = min_C g > 0.
For ω admissible in G: (1 − χ)ω vanishes on N, so X(ω) = X(χω); χω is admissible in V since |χω| = χ|ω| ≤ 1.
Hence ofReal(X(ω)) ≤ M_V(X); take the supremum.

Reused declaration: this is the already comparator-accepted theorem lcmp_massOn_le_add_of_eval_eq (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.local_comparison-a1.mass_triangle-a1), reused here with its identical frozen Lean type; in the present decomposition it is the subadditivity M(∂T'_j) ≤ M(B_{j,r}) + M(Z_{j,r}) of step 6 of the parent-supplied proof of cbr_closure_succ (∂T'_j = B_{j,r} + Z_{j,r}). The numbered proof is the one reviewed for that node.

1. Let ω be admissible for M_G: ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Then −ω is admissible as well: tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω, and |−ω(x)| = |ω(x)| because the Euclidean coefficient norm is invariant under α ↦ −α (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
2. By the definition of M_G as a supremum, ofReal(X(ω)) ≤ M_G(X), ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ M_G(Y) and ofReal(Y(−ω)) ≤ M_G(Y); by linearity Y(−ω) = −Y(ω). Hence ofReal(|Y(ω)|) ≤ M_G(Y) (|Y(ω)| is Y(ω) or −Y(ω)).
3. c·Y(ω) ≤ |c·Y(ω)| = |c|·|Y(ω)| ≤ |Y(ω)|, so by hypothesis Z(ω) = X(ω) + c·Y(ω) ≤ X(ω) + |Y(ω)|. Since ofReal is monotone and ofReal(p + q) ≤ ofReal(p) + ofReal(q) for all real p, q (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le): ofReal(Z(ω)) ≤ ofReal(X(ω)) + ofReal(|Y(ω)|) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y).
4. Taking the supremum over all admissible ω gives M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y). ∎
proof_key_steps: For ω admissible in G, −ω is admissible too, so ofReal(|Y(ω)|) ≤ M_G(Y).
c·Y(ω) ≤ |Y(ω)| since |c| ≤ 1, so ofReal(Z(ω)) ≤ ofReal(X(ω)) + ofReal(|Y(ω)|) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y).
Take the supremum over admissible ω.

subproblems.title: Measure calculus of integer multiplicity representations and of their restrictions to Borel sets (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation in U (contract IMRep U n) with weight μ_R := θ Hⁿ⌞M (contract R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ, Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then (a) μ_R is absolutely continuous with respect to Hⁿ⌞M; (b) ξ is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable; (c) for every Borel set E and every IMRep R′ in U with carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ: μ_{R′} = μ_R⌞E, and for every n-form ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ (no regularity assumed) the action R′(ω) = ∫_{M∩E} θ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ (contract IMRep.action) equals ∫_E ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dμ_R(x) (Bochner integrals).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), R.measure ≪ μHE[n].restrict R.carrier ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable R.orient R.measure ∧ ∀ (E : Set (Euclid P)) (R' : IMRep U n), MeasurableSet E → R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E → R'.mult = R.mult → R'.orient = R.orient → R'.measure = R.measure.restrict E ∧ ∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, R'.action ω = ∫ x in E, R.orient x (ω x) ∂R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused declaration: this is the already comparator-accepted theorem lcmp_imRep_measure_restrict (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.local_comparison-a1.imrep_restriction-a1), reused here with its identical frozen Lean type; in the present decomposition it supplies step 2 (“by (IMC)(d) the pairs (μ_j, ξ_j) … are admissible representations of T_j”) and step 6 (the IM restriction (M_j ∩ B_r(x₀), θ_j, ξ_j) has values ∫_{M_j∩B_r(x₀)} θ_jξ_j(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_{f<r} ξ_j(ω) dμ_j) of the parent-supplied proof of cbr_closure_succ. The numbered proof is the one reviewed for that node; openness of U is not needed.

Notation: ν := Hⁿ⌞M, so μ_R = ν.withDensity θ, where θ : ℝ^P → ℕ is Borel (IMRep field measurable_mult) and is used as a density through the cast ℕ → [0, ∞).

1. (a) A measure with a density with respect to ν is absolutely continuous with respect to ν (Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous): if ν(N) = 0 then μ_R(N) = ∫_N θ dν = 0.
2. (b) The IMRep field aestronglyMeasurable_orient says that ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for ν. By (a), every ν-null set is μ_R-null, so ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for μ_R (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac).
3. (c), weights. Let E be Borel and R′ as in the statement. Restriction to a measurable set commutes with taking a density, and restrictions compose: (ν.withDensity θ)⌞E = (ν⌞E).withDensity θ (restrict_withDensity) and ν⌞E = (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞E = Hⁿ⌞(E ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Hence μ_R⌞E = (Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E)).withDensity θ = μ_{R′}, because R′ has carrier M ∩ E and multiplicity θ.
4. (c), actions. The map x ↦ θ(x) ∈ [0, ∞) is Borel (a Borel map into ℕ followed by a map out of the discrete space ℕ). For any measure λ, any Borel density g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞) and any function h : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫ h d(λ.withDensity g) = ∫ g·h dλ as Bochner integrals, without any integrability assumption (Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul; if one side is not integrable, neither is the other and both integrals are 0). Apply this with λ = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E), g = θ and h(x) = ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩: by step 3, ∫_E ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_{R′} = ∫_{M∩E} θ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ, and the last integral is R′(ω) by the definition of IMRep.action for R′ (carrier M ∩ E, multiplicity θ, orientation ξ). ∎
proof_key_steps: μ_R = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, hence ξ is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable.
(ν.withDensity θ)⌞E = (ν⌞E).withDensity θ and (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞E = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E), so μ_R⌞E = μ_{R′}.
∫ h d(λ.withDensity θ) = ∫ θ h dλ (no integrability needed) turns ∫_E ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R into ∫_{M∩E} θ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = R′(ω).

subproblems.title: Local finiteness of Hⁿ⌞M and of the weight of an integer multiplicity representation (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation in U (an IMRep U n): M = R.carrier is Borel with M ⊆ U; θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ is Borel with θ ≥ 1 on M; and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, where Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Let μ_R = R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ. Then for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ U: Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ and μ_R(K) < ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (R.carrier ∩ K) ≠ ∞ ∧ R.measure K ≠ ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused declaration: this is the already comparator-accepted theorem rsd_imrep_compact_measure_ne_top (node root.regular_set_dense-a1.density_eq_multiplicity-a1.imrep_local_finiteness-a1), reused here with its identical frozen Lean type; in the present decomposition it supplies the local finiteness μ_j(K) < ∞ (compact K ⊆ U) of the IMRep weights μ_j required by (SL) and (T2) in steps 2–7 of the parent-supplied proof of cbr_closure_succ. The numbered proof is the one reviewed for that node; it is the standing hypothesis of Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1 (θ locally Hⁿ-integrable), encoded by the IMRep fields mult_pos and locallyIntegrable_mult.

Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P (Euclid P); M = R.carrier; θ(x) = R.mult x ∈ ℕ ⊆ [0, ∞]; μ_R = R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ. Fix a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ U.

1. K is a compact subset of the Hausdorff space ℝ^P, hence closed, hence Borel (IsCompact.measurableSet).
2. (Weight of K.) Since K is measurable, μ_R(K) = ∫_K θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) by the definition of withDensity (withDensity_apply), and (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞K = Hⁿ⌞(K ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Hence μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ, after commuting the intersection.
3. The IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult, applied to the compact set K ⊆ U, gives ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≠ ∞. By step 2, μ_R(K) ≠ ∞. This is the second conclusion.
4. (θ ≥ 1 on M.) For x ∈ M ∩ K, the field mult_pos gives 0 < R.mult x in ℕ. Hence 1 ≤ R.mult x, and after casting to [0, ∞], 1 ≤ θ(x).
5. (Measurability.) θ is measurable: it is the composition of the measurable map R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ (field measurable_mult) with the cast ℕ → [0, ∞], and every map out of the discrete space ℕ is measurable (measurable_from_nat).
6. (Unweighted measure.) Hⁿ(M ∩ K) = ∫_{M∩K} 1 dHⁿ (setLIntegral_one). This is at most ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ by monotonicity of the set lower integral (setLIntegral_mono), using the pointwise bound of step 4 on M ∩ K and the measurability of step 5. The right side is finite by step 3, so Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≠ ∞. This is the first conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: A compact K is closed, hence Borel.
μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ by withDensity_apply and restrict_restrict; this is finite by locallyIntegrable_mult.
θ ≥ 1 on M (mult_pos) gives Hⁿ(M ∩ K) = ∫_{M∩K} 1 dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞.

subproblems.title: Integral formula T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R for an integer multiplicity triple (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) : IMRep U n, and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n: a C^∞ n-form on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U). Let μ_R = R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ. Then the function x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ_R-integrable, and R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) equals ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ_R(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Integrable (fun x => R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x)) R.measure ∧ R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) = ∫ x, R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂R.measure
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused declaration: this is the already comparator-accepted theorem dor_ims_action_eq_integral (node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1.action_integral_formula-a1), reused here with its identical frozen Lean type; in the present decomposition it supplies the representation T_j(ω) = ∫ ξ_j(ω) dμ_j of step 2 of the parent-supplied proof of cbr_closure_succ (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 (‡) and 3.2(3)). The numbered proof is the one reviewed for that node.

Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, ν := μHE[n].restrict M = Hⁿ⌞M, μ := R.measure = ν.withDensity (x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ≥0∞)), f(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)), K := tsupport ω. For an n-covector α, ‖α‖ is its operator norm as a continuous alternating map.

1. ω is C^∞, hence continuous, and has compact support. So K is compact, closed and Borel, and K ⊆ U because ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
2. θ is measurable (R.measurable_mult; ℕ carries the discrete σ-algebra), so x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ≥0) is measurable. A measure with a density is absolutely continuous, so μ ≪ ν (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous).
3. (Measurability.) ξ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient), hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable since μ ≪ ν. ω is continuous, hence strongly measurable. Evaluation Λₙ × Λⁿ → ℝ, (ζ, α) ↦ ζ(α), is continuous (bounded bilinear; isBoundedBilinearMap_apply.continuous). So f is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂).
4. (Pointwise bound.) By R.orients, for ν-a.e. x (hence μ-a.e. x) there are an orthonormal family τ and s ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(x)(α) = s·α(τ) for all α. Then |f(x)| = |ω(x)(τ)| ≤ ‖ω(x)‖·∏_j ‖τ_j‖ = ‖ω(x)‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm). Since ω is continuous with compact support, there is C with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ C for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). If x ∉ K then ω(x) = 0, so f(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0. Hence |f| ≤ C·1_K μ-a.e.
5. (Finiteness.) Since K is measurable, μ(K) = ∫_K θ dν = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ, which is finite by R.locallyIntegrable_mult, as K is compact and K ⊆ U. So C·1_K is μ-integrable, and by step 3 and domination (Integrable.mono'), f is μ-integrable.
6. (Integral identity.) For measurable g : ℝ^P → ℝ≥0 and any function h, ∫ h d(ν.withDensity g) = ∫ g(x)·h(x) dν(x) (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul; no integrability hypothesis is needed). Take g = θ, noting (θ(x) : ℝ≥0∞) = ((θ(x) : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0∞). Then ∫ f dμ = ∫ θ(x)·f(x) dν(x) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) = R.action ω. Together with step 5 this proves both claims. ∎
proof_key_steps: f(x) = ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable: ξ is, μ_R ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, and evaluation is continuous.
μ_R-a.e. |f| ≤ ‖ω‖ ≤ C·1_{spt ω}, because ξ(x) = ±ev_τ with τ orthonormal.
μ_R(spt ω) = ∫_{M∩spt ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by locallyIntegrable_mult, so f is integrable.
∫ f dμ_R = ∫_M θ f dHⁿ = R.action ω by the withDensity integral formula.

subproblems.title: Good radius: a level in (ρ, ρ′) with a prescribed a.e. property, a μ-null sphere and a Markov bound (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on (the Borel sets of) ℝ^P, y ∈ ℝ^P, and ρ < ρ′ real numbers. Let g : ℝ → [0, ∞] be L¹-a.e. measurable (L¹ = Lebesgue measure on ℝ), let I ∈ [0, ∞] with ∫_ℝ g dL¹ ≤ I (lower Lebesgue integral), and let p be a property of real numbers holding for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ. Assume μ(B̄_{ρ′}(y)) < ∞. Then there is t ∈ ℝ with ρ < t < ρ′ such that p(t) holds, μ(∂B_t(y)) = 0, where ∂B_t(y) = {x ∈ ℝ^P : |x − y| = t} (Metric.sphere y t), and g(t) ≤ (2/(ρ′ − ρ))·I, the product being computed in [0, ∞] as ENNReal.ofReal(2/(ρ′ − ρ))·I.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P) (ρ ρ' : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (I : ℝ≥0∞) (p : ℝ → Prop), ρ < ρ' → μ (closedBall y ρ') ≠ ∞ → AEMeasurable g → ∫⁻ t, g t ≤ I → (∀ᵐ t, p t) → ∃ t : ℝ, ρ < t ∧ t < ρ' ∧ p t ∧ μ (sphere y t) = 0 ∧ g t ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 / (ρ' - ρ)) * I
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused declaration: this is the already comparator-accepted theorem dor_lmb_glc_good_radius (node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.limsup_mass_bound-a1.level_cut-a1.good_radius-a1), reused here with its identical frozen Lean type; in the present decomposition it is the choice of the radius in step 4 of the parent-supplied proof of cbr_closure_succ (“liminf_j M_G(Z_{j,r}) < ∞ for a.e. r ∈ (0, r₀); also μ(∂B_r(x₀)) = 0 for all but countably many r; fix r with both properties”). The numbered proof is the one reviewed for that node. Notation: J := (ρ, ρ′), δ := ρ′ − ρ > 0, c := ofReal(2/δ) ∈ [0, ∞]; L¹ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, used as an outer measure (monotone and countably subadditive on arbitrary subsets of ℝ); ∂B_s := ∂B_s(y) = {x : |x − y| = s}, B̄_s := B̄_s(y).

1. Facts about c. Since 2/δ > 0 we have c ≠ 0, and c ≠ ∞ because ofReal is finite. Moreover c⁻¹ = ofReal((2/δ)⁻¹) = ofReal(δ/2) (ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos and (2/δ)⁻¹ = δ/2).
2. The exceptional set of p. Let N₁ := {t ∈ ℝ : p(t) fails}. Since p holds L¹-a.e., L¹(N₁) = 0 (ae_iff).
3. Charged spheres. Let ν := μ⌞B̄_{ρ′}, i.e. ν(A) = μ(A ∩ B̄_{ρ′}) for Borel A. Then ν(ℝ^P) = μ(B̄_{ρ′}) < ∞, so ν is a finite (hence s-finite) measure (isFiniteMeasure_restrict). The spheres ∂B_s, s ∈ ℝ, are closed, hence Borel, and pairwise disjoint: if x ∈ ∂B_s ∩ ∂B_{s′} then s = |x − y| = s′. For an s-finite measure only countably many members of a pairwise disjoint family of measurable sets have positive measure (Measure.countable_meas_pos_of_disjoint_iUnion). Hence N₂ := {s ∈ ℝ : 0 < ν(∂B_s)} is countable, and L¹(N₂) = 0 because L¹ has no atoms (Set.Countable.measure_zero). Moreover, if s ≤ ρ′ then ∂B_s ⊆ B̄_s ⊆ B̄_{ρ′}, so ν(∂B_s) = μ(∂B_s ∩ B̄_{ρ′}) = μ(∂B_s) (Measure.restrict_apply for the closed set ∂B_s).
4. The Markov set. Let N₃ := {t ∈ ℝ : c·I < g(t)}. We show L¹(N₃) ≤ ofReal(δ/2) by cases on I. (a) I = 0. Then ∫ g dL¹ ≤ 0, so ∫ g dL¹ = 0, and since g is a.e.-measurable, g = 0 L¹-a.e. (lintegral_eq_zero_iff′). As c·I = 0, every t ∈ N₃ has g(t) > 0, so N₃ ⊆ {t : g(t) ≠ 0}, an L¹-null set; hence L¹(N₃) = 0 ≤ ofReal(δ/2). (b) I = ∞. Since c ≠ 0, c·I = ∞ (ENNReal.mul_top), and no t satisfies ∞ < g(t). So N₃ = ∅ and L¹(N₃) = 0 ≤ ofReal(δ/2). (c) I ≠ 0 and I ≠ ∞. Put ε := c·I; then ε ≠ 0 (as c ≠ 0 and I ≠ 0) and ε ≠ ∞ (as c ≠ ∞ and I ≠ ∞). Since N₃ ⊆ {t : ε ≤ g(t)}, Markov's inequality for the a.e.-measurable g (meas_ge_le_lintegral_div) gives L¹(N₃) ≤ L¹({ε ≤ g}) ≤ (∫ g dL¹)/ε ≤ I/(c·I). Finally I/(c·I) = (c·I)⁻¹·I = c⁻¹·(I⁻¹·I) = c⁻¹ (ENNReal.mul_inv, using c ≠ 0 and c ≠ ∞, and I⁻¹·I = 1 since I ≠ 0, ∞), and c⁻¹ = ofReal(δ/2) by step 1. Hence L¹(N₃) ≤ ofReal(δ/2).
5. Covering. Suppose, for a contradiction, that no t satisfies ρ < t < ρ′, p(t), μ(∂B_t) = 0 and g(t) ≤ c·I. Then J ⊆ N₁ ∪ N₂ ∪ N₃: otherwise take t ∈ J outside N₁ ∪ N₂ ∪ N₃. Then p(t) holds (t ∉ N₁); ν(∂B_t) = 0 (t ∉ N₂), hence μ(∂B_t) = ν(∂B_t) = 0 by step 3 because t < ρ′; and g(t) ≤ c·I (t ∉ N₃). So t has all four properties, contradicting the assumption.
6. By monotonicity and subadditivity of L¹ and steps 2–4, ofReal(δ) = L¹(J) ≤ L¹(N₁) + L¹(N₂) + L¹(N₃) ≤ 0 + 0 + ofReal(δ/2) = ofReal(δ/2) (Real.volume_Ioo). Since δ/2 ≥ 0, this gives δ ≤ δ/2 (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff), i.e. δ ≤ 0, contradicting δ > 0.
7. Hence there is t with ρ < t < ρ′, p(t), μ(∂B_t(y)) = 0 and g(t) ≤ ofReal(2/(ρ′ − ρ))·I. ∎
proof_key_steps: N₁ := {t : ¬p(t)} is L¹-null; N₂ := {s : μ⌞B̄_{ρ′}(y)(∂B_s(y)) > 0} is countable (pairwise disjoint closed spheres, finite measure), hence L¹-null; μ⌞B̄_{ρ′}(y) and μ agree on ∂B_s(y) for s ≤ ρ′.
N₃ := {t : (2/(ρ′−ρ))·I < g(t)} has L¹-measure ≤ (ρ′−ρ)/2: if I = 0 then g = 0 a.e.; if I = ∞ then N₃ = ∅; otherwise Markov’s inequality with ε = (2/(ρ′−ρ))·I.
If no good t existed, (ρ, ρ′) ⊆ N₁ ∪ N₂ ∪ N₃, so ρ′ − ρ ≤ 0 + 0 + (ρ′ − ρ)/2, a contradiction.

subproblems.title: Localization at a point (Simon 6.8.3(1)): IM restrictions to a ball with bounded masses and boundary masses converging to T⌞B_r(x₀)
subproblems.statement: Assume (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL) and (TOOLS); they appear verbatim as hypotheses of the Lean statement. (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL) are the exact frozen statements of cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub and cmc_slice_mass_bounds (dependencies of the grandparent node), and (TOOLS) = (T1) ∧ (T2) ∧ (MM) is the exact frozen statement of cbr_measure_convergence_tools (a dependency of the parent cbr_closure_succ). In words: (REP) a current X ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, with M_W(X) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U has a representation (μ, ξ): μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, μ(W) = M_W(X) for open W, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x and α, and X(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (plus an Hⁿ-null-set clause not used here); (MR) M_W(X) = R.measure(W) for every IMRep R in open U representing X and every open W; (IMC) (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces, (b) for an IMRep R in open U and a Borel set E there are a current A and an IMRep R′ representing A with carrier R.carrier ∩ E, multiplicity R.mult and orientation R.orient, (c) differences of IM currents are IM, (d) for every IMRep R, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for Hⁿ⌞R.carrier-a.e. x and all α; (SL) for X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), U open, with admissible representations (μ, ξ) of X and (μ′, ξ′) of ∂X (measures finite on compact subsets of U, a.e. strongly measurable fields with a.e. bound |·| ≤ 1) and an L-Lipschitz f there are currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_k(U) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ′(η) dμ′, ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) when tsupport η ∩ {f = t} = ∅, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for open W, and an integrated bound; (T1) a sequence of measures with sup_j μ_j(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (U open) has a subsequence μ_{φ(j)} and a measure μ with μ(K) < ∞ and limsup_j μ_{φ(j)}(K) ≤ μ(K) for compact K ⊆ U (and further properties); (T2) if X_j ⇀ X in 𝒟_k(U), (μ_j, ξ_j) and (μ_X, ξ_X) are admissible representations of X_j and X, μ is finite on compact subsets of U with limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K), f is continuous and μ{f = t} = 0, then ∫_{f<t} ξ_j(ω) dμ_j → ∫_{f<t} ξ_X(ω) dμ_X for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U); (MM) if μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞, f is continuous and Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for t ∈ (a, b), then there is a measurable g ≥ 0 with liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for L¹-a.e. t ∈ (a, b) and ∫_{(a,b)} g ≤ L·liminf_j μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}). Let d, P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T_j, T ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) with every T_j integer multiplicity, sup_j (M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure contained in U (boundaryMassOn(T_j, W) = M_W(∂T_j) in degree d + 1), T_j ⇀ T in U, and x₀ ∈ U. Then there are r > 0 with closedBall(x₀, r) ⊆ U, currents S_j ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U), IMReps R′_j in U and A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) such that: R′_j represents S_j and R′_j.carrier ⊆ closedBall(x₀, r); S_j(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω is disjoint from closedBall(x₀, r); sup_j (M(S_j) + M(∂S_j)) < ∞ (total masses in U, M = massOn U); S_j ⇀ A in U; and A(ω) = T(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(x₀, r).

Source: the parent-supplied proof of cbr_closure_succ, steps 1–7 (Part V, V2 of the grandparent proof; Simon Ch. 6, Remark 8.3(1)), specialised to one point x₀. (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (TOOLS) = (T1) ∧ (T2) ∧ (MM) are hypotheses (exact frozen statements). Sibling dependencies (comparator-accepted declarations reused with their exact frozen types):
- VOM = lcmp_massOn_le_of_vanish_off_compact (key vanish_off_mass): if C is compact, V open, C ⊆ V and X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ C = ∅, then M_G(X) ≤ M_V(X) for every set G;
- TRI = lcmp_massOn_le_add_of_eval_eq (key mass_triangle): if |c| ≤ 1 and Z(ω) = X(ω) + c·Y(ω) for every ω with tsupport ω ⊆ G, then M_G(Z) ≤ M_G(X) + M_G(Y);
- IR = lcmp_imRep_measure_restrict (key imrep_restrict): for an IMRep R, R.measure ≪ Hⁿ⌞R.carrier, R.orient is R.measure-a.e. strongly measurable, and for Borel E and an IMRep R′ with carrier R.carrier ∩ E, multiplicity R.mult and orientation R.orient, R′.action(ω) = ∫_E R.orient(ω) dR.measure for every n-form ω;
- ICF = rsd_imrep_compact_measure_ne_top (key imrep_compact_finite): R.measure(K) ≠ ∞ for compact K ⊆ U;
- IAI = dor_ims_action_eq_integral (key imrep_action_integral): R.action(ω) = ∫ R.orient(ω) dR.measure for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U);
- GR = dor_lmb_glc_good_radius (key good_radius): if ρ < ρ′, μ(closedBall(y, ρ′)) ≠ ∞, g : ℝ → [0, ∞] is a.e. measurable with ∫ g dL¹ ≤ I and p holds L¹-a.e., then some t ∈ (ρ, ρ′) has p(t), μ(sphere(y, t)) = 0 and g(t) ≤ ofReal(2/(ρ′ − ρ))·I.
Notation: n := d + 1; for X of degree n, boundaryMassOn(X, W) = M_W(∂X) (definitional in degree d + 1); M(X) := X.mass = M_U(X) (definition of total mass on the domain U); f(x) := dist(x, x₀), continuous and 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.dist_left); {f < t} = ball(x₀, t) and {f = t} = sphere(x₀, t) (definitions of Metric.ball and Metric.sphere). Simplification relative to the supplied step 2: the admissible representation of ∂T_j needed by (SL) is taken from (REP) applied to ∂T_j instead of an IMRep of ∂T_j produced by BR(d); (SL) only needs an admissible representation.

0. (Mass of a set-integral current; used in steps 9(c) and 9(d).) Claim: let k ∈ ℕ, s ⊆ ℝ^P, X ∈ 𝒟_k(U), ν a measure on ℝ^P and v : ℝ^P → Λ_k with |v(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every k-covector α for ν-a.e. x; if X(ω) = ∫_s v(x)(ω(x)) dν(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), then M(X) ≤ ν(s). Proof: let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) be admissible for M(X) = M_U(X), i.e. |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. For ν-a.e. x, hence for ν⌞s-a.e. x, |v(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1. Then ofReal(X(ω)) = ofReal(∫_s v(ω) dν) ≤ ofReal(|∫_s v(ω) dν|) = ‖∫_s v(ω) dν‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_s ‖v(ω)‖ₑ dν (Mathlib enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm, valid without any integrability or measurability assumption) ≤ ∫⁻_s 1 dν (lintegral_mono_ae) = ν(s) (setLIntegral_const; ν⌞s(ℝ^P) = ν(s) for every set s). M(X) is the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over the admissible ω, so M(X) ≤ ν(s).
1. (Radius r₀, the set G and the bound Λ.) U is open and x₀ ∈ U, so there is ε > 0 with ball(x₀, ε) ⊆ U; put r₀ := ε/2 > 0, so closedBall(x₀, r₀) ⊆ ball(x₀, ε) ⊆ U. Let G := ball(x₀, r₀). G is open and closure G ⊆ closedBall(x₀, r₀) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall), so closure G is compact (a closed subset of a compact set) and contained in U: G ⊂⊂ U. Put Λ := sup_j (M_G(T_j) + M_G(∂T_j)), finite by hypothesis (W := G). Then M_G(T_j) ≤ Λ and M_G(∂T_j) ≤ Λ for every j.
2. (Locally finite masses.) Let W be open with W ⊂⊂ U and Λ_W := sup_j (M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞. Then M_W(∂T_j) ≤ Λ_W for every j. Since T_j ⇀ T, also ∂T_j ⇀ ∂T (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary), and lower semicontinuity of mass (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf) gives M_W(T) ≤ liminf_j M_W(T_j) ≤ limsup_j M_W(T_j) ≤ sup_j M_W(T_j) ≤ Λ_W < ∞, and likewise M_W(∂T) ≤ liminf_j M_W(∂T_j) ≤ Λ_W < ∞.
3. (Representations.) (a) For each j, (REP) applied to ∂T_j ∈ 𝒟_d(U), which has locally finite mass by step 2, gives a measure μ′_j and ξ′_j : ℝ^P → Λ_d with μ′_j(W) = M_W(∂T_j) for open W, μ′_j(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, ξ′_j μ′_j-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ′_j(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x and α, and ∂T_j(η) = ∫ ξ′_j(η) dμ′_j for η ∈ 𝒟^d(U). (b) (REP) applied to T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and to ∂T ∈ 𝒟_d(U) (step 2) gives (μ_T, ξ_T) and (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}) with the same properties; in particular T(ω) = ∫ ξ_T(ω) dμ_T for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). (c) For each j choose an IMRep R_j = (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) in U representing T_j (hypothesis) and put μ_j := R_j.measure. Then μ_j(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (ICF); μ_j ≪ Hⁿ⌞M_j and ξ_j is μ_j-a.e. strongly measurable (IR); the fourth conjunct (IMC)(d) of (IMC) gives |ξ_j(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α for Hⁿ⌞M_j-a.e. x, hence for μ_j-a.e. x by absolute continuity; T_j(ω) = R_j.action(ω) = ∫ ξ_j(ω) dμ_j for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (R_j represents T_j, then IAI); and μ_j(W) = M_W(T_j) for every open W ((MR)).
4. (Uniform bounds on compact sets.) Let K ⊆ U be compact. There is an open W with K ⊆ W, closure W compact and closure W ⊆ U (Mathlib exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure); so W ⊂⊂ U, and μ_j(K) ≤ μ_j(W) = M_W(T_j) ≤ Λ_W for every j. Hence sup_j μ_j(K) < ∞.
5. (Measure compactness.) (T1) applied to (μ_j) in U gives a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and a measure μ with μ(K) < ∞ and limsup_j μ_{φ(j)}(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ U.
6. (Slicing.) For each j apply (SL) with k := d, the current T_{φ(j)}, (μ, ξ) := (μ_{φ(j)}, ξ_{φ(j)}), (μ′, ξ′) := (μ′_{φ(j)}, ξ′_{φ(j)}), the function f and L := 1; its hypotheses are steps 3(a) and 3(c) (the everywhere bound for ξ′_{φ(j)} implies the a.e. bound). This gives currents A_j(t) ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and B_j(t) ∈ 𝒟_d(U), t ∈ ℝ, with (i) A_j(t)(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ_{φ(j)}(ω) dμ_{φ(j)}; (ii) B_j(t)(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ′_{φ(j)}(η) dμ′_{φ(j)}; (iii) ∂A_j(t)(η) = B_j(t)(η) whenever tsupport η ∩ {f = t} = ∅; (iv) for every open W, M_W(Z_j(t)) ≤ 1·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ_{φ(j)}(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}), where Z_j(t) := ∂A_j(t) − B_j(t) ∈ 𝒟_d(U). Likewise (SL) applied to T with (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}), f and L := 1 (step 3(b)) gives currents A_T(t) ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with A_T(t)(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ_T(ω) dμ_T.
7. (Measurable majorant.) Put z_j(t) := M_G(Z_j(t)). Apply (MM) to the measures μ_{φ(j)}, f, G, a := 0, b := r₀, L := 1 and z: f is continuous; μ_{φ(j)}(G ∩ {0 < f < r₀}) ≤ μ_{φ(j)}(G) = M_G(T_{φ(j)}) ≤ Λ < ∞; and z_j(t) ≤ 1·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ_{φ(j)}(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) by 6(iv) with W := G. (MM) gives a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with liminf_j z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for L¹-a.e. t ∈ (0, r₀) and ∫_{(0,r₀)} g dL¹ ≤ 1·liminf_j μ_{φ(j)}(G ∩ {0 < f < r₀}) ≤ Λ (every term is at most μ_{φ(j)}(G) = M_G(T_{φ(j)}) ≤ Λ, and liminf ≤ limsup ≤ sup).
